item.title: Tai Po fire: Gov’t investigative committee urges witnesses to submit info, photos of deadly Hong Kong blaze
item.description: A government committee investigating the Tai Po fire that killed 168 people last November is inviting witnesses and other members of the public to provide information about the tragedy. item.title: Man arrested for allegedly assaulting wheelchair-bound bus passenger who refused seatbelt, as new rules kick in
item.description: A 53-year-old man has been arrested for allegedly assaulting an elderly wheelchair-bound bus passenger who refused to fasten his seatbelt and delayed the man’s commute, according to police. item.title: China defence minister vows greater ‘strategic coordination’ with Russia
item.description: China’s Defence Minister Dong Jun told his Russian counterpart that the two countries should “strengthen strategic coordination” during a video call on Tuesday, according to state broadcaster CCTV. The call came days after negotiators from Russia and Ukraine met to discuss a US-brokered plan to end the war — nearly four years after Moscow’s invasion […]

item.description: Hong Kong politician Regina Ip has engaged in a fiery text message exchange with a veteran of the city’s biggest political party after a lawmaker from Ip’s own party was filmed driving against the flow of traffic last week. item.title: Pok Fu Lam construction workers scale scaffolding in protest over unpaid wages from firm linked to Tai Po fire
item.description: Construction workers at a residential estate in Pok Fu Lam have staged a protest demanding unpaid wages after their project – managed by a contractor linked to the Wang Fuk Court fire – was halted following the blaze. item.title: UK’s Keir Starmer arrives in China to defend ‘pragmatic’ partnership, expected to raise Jimmy Lai issue
item.description: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer arrived in Beijing on Wednesday to meet with Chinese leader Xi Jinping, hoping to restore long fraught relations. item.title: 6 months’ jail for PolyU applicant who shoved HK$50k bribe into lecturer’s pocket
item.description: A 39-year-old businessman has been jailed for six months after offering a HK$50,000 bribe to a senior Hong Kong Polytechnic University (PolyU) lecturer. item.title: Hong Kong mulls legislation to tackle AI ‘deepfake’ porn – official
item.description: An inter-departmental working group set up by Hong Kong’s justice department is studying whether to set up legislation for cases involving indecent images generated by Artificial Intelligence (AI), following an AI-porn scandal at a local university. item.description: Around HK$4.5 billion has been raised in the Hong Kong government’s public donation fund for victims of the deadly Tai Po fire.
